content.title: About
content.content: Eggplant Parmesan Casserole is a layered dish made with baked eggplant slices, tomato sauce, Parmesan cheese and often mozzarella. It combines tender vegetables, creamy cheese, and aromatic herbs for a hearty, flavorful take on the classic Italian casserole.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggplant has been cultivated for over 4,000 years and is one of the oldest known vegetables.
The dish originates from southern Italy, where eggplants grow abundantly.
Authentic Parmesan used in the recipe is aged at least 12 months, giving it a distinct nutty flavor.
It is a popular vegetarian main course in many Mediterranean cuisines.
The casserole can be prepared ahead of time and reheated, making it convenient for family meals.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Eggplant provides fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When made with reduced‑fat cheese, the casserole remains moderately low in calories.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Eggplant contains antioxidants such as nasunin that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin K
items.content: Parmesan adds calcium and vitamin K, important for bone health and blood clotting.

items.title: Heart‑friendly fats
items.content: Olive oil, commonly used in the recipe, provides monounsaturated fats that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Parmesan cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with dairy sensitivities.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Hard cheese and prepared tomato sauce can be high in sodium; people with hypertension should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Eggplant contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the eggplant, lightly pan‑fry or bake the slices, then layer them with tomato sauce, cheese, and herbs. Bake until the top is golden and bubbly. Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil or parsley.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the casserole to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to restore the crispy crust.
